K-means minimises the distance
to the nearest centroid only.

Here 9 of 16 centroids sit in the
dashed circle, 13% of the area.
Tail items far out share a few
centroids → same semantic ID.

FSQ rounds each dimension to
fixed levels: the grid does not
depend on the data, so sparse
regions keep their own cells.
In QARM's 3-level Res-Kmeans, more than 30% of semantic IDs map to several items (Shopping).
